reviews.review: Played. died. Played Again but better. Still died. Would recommend.
Personally I have hugely enjoyed the exploration and discovery, even over multiple playthroughs. Secrets abound, tons of gear encourage build crafting. Gunplay is tight and multiplayer.

First off, this is a solid 8/10 game. It'd be higher but the ending has huge problems.

This is a really interesting concept for a game, where it sends you into a variety of worlds with all sorts of different plots and fundamental backstories. I'd like to call this GURPS the video game (look it up). The only shame is that there aren't even more. Perhaps we'll get more by DLC, or have a Remnant 3 to look forward to.

Fantastic hybrid shooter/Soulslike gameplay style that feels very engaging and flexible to explore how you want to play it. 

Great world setpieces with a surprising number of plotlines and lore for any given world instance, procedurally assembled on each run.

Really solid, coherent graphics for all of the different aesthetics they're pulling together. 

Unfortunately have to dock it points for the last chapter, where the story absolutely ♥♥♥♥♥ the bed. It was painful enough to actively ruin some of my feelings for this game. If I revisit it, I'll probably just pretend that this chapter didn't exist.

This game is a wonderful delight to those who love looter shooters, lore, and exploration. 
It starts off with a slow introduction but once you're out of the tutorial level the game frees you to try and learn absolutely everything from in-game merchants to upgrades that won't be needed until several hours into the game. It doesn't hold the player's hand for many of the in-game mechanics like Mutators, archetypes, and varying pieces of gameplay but it does enough to steer the player to be curious about them. 
I had a blast playing through this game with my Fiancee and we're continuing to do so. I think one degree of frustration I felt was with the location of some archetypes as it felt like the devs didn't want you to find some of them (Engineer, Archon..) or absolutely random invisible walls, but the the game provided through exploration and combat supersceded this lingering headache. 

7/10. Game is great for short-medium burts of gameplay.
PROS: Fun customization for weapon abilities. Class/archetype differences make you feel unique when paired with others and keep gameplay fresh. The worlds are varied and different from one another while also keeping a familiar visual appeal. The game provides enough information to work with everything. 
CONS: Archetypes are too hard to achieve for something that is a GAME CHANGING mechanic (I understand working together with players online, but an archetype hidden behind a cloud of death that has a completely inconspicuous location? That's just frustrating). Character customization is lacking. Music design is very bland/I can't recognize most pieces of music because it's all the same level of noise - AKA there's no change in the volume of anything. It's all either super loud or super soft, never crescendo nor de-crescendos to build tension/excitement. 

I recommend playing with a friend. Friendly fire is a thing but it makes the game all the more fun :)
